I see the issue - the web_fetch returns only partial content (truncated at 20000 chars). Let me handle this properly by fetching individual paper pages which will be shorter. First, let me parse what we have and then fetch details for specific papers.

```python
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

# Parse the XML we got from the web_fetch
full_xml = result['content']
root = ET.fromstring(full_xml)
ns = {'atom': 'http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom'}

entries = root.findall('atom:entry', ns)
papers_parsed = []
for entry in entries:
    title = entry.find('atom:title', ns).text.strip().replace('\n', ' ')
    paper_id = entry.find('atom:id', ns).text.split('/abs/')[-1]
    summary = entry.find('atom:summary', ns).text.strip().replace('\n', ' ')
    published = entry.find('atom:published', ns).text
    authors = [a.find('atom:name', ns).text for a in entry.findall('atom:author', ns)]
    papers_parsed.append({
        'title': title,
        'arxiv_id': paper_id,
        'summary': summary,
        'published': published,
        'authors': authors
    })

print(f"Parsed {len(papers_parsed)} papers from XML")
for i, p in enumerate(papers_parsed):
    print(f"\n[{i+1}] {p['title']}")
    print(f"    ID: {p['arxiv_id']}")
    print(f"    Date: {p['published'][:10]}")
    print(f"    Authors: {', '.join(p['authors'][:3])}...")
    print(f"    Summary (first 200): {p['summary'][:200]}")
```
